verdict.rationale: The lexical data pulls in two directions and supports no single reading. Eph 2:11-22 lexically describes Jew and Gentile fused into one new man (ἕνα καινὸν ἄνθρωπον) and reconciled in one body (ἑνὶ σώματι), with the dividing wall (μεσότοιχον τοῦ φραγμοῦ) abolished (καταργήσας, aorist active participle of καταργέω, render inoperative), and Gal 3:28-29 calls believers one (εἷς) in Christ and Abraham's seed (σπέρμα), which favors continuity and merger. But Rom 11:25-29 keeps πᾶς Ἰσραήλ as a future-saved entity distinct from the πλήρωμα τῶν ἐθνῶν, with gifts and calling irrevocable (ἀμεταμέλητα), and Rom 11:17-24 calls Israel the natural branches (κατὰ φύσιν) of the cultivated olive tree (ἐλαία) into which wild Gentile branches (ἀγριέλαιος) are grafted, which favors an enduring distinction within ONE tree. The naming term οἰκονομία (Eph 1:10, Eph 3:2, Eph 3:9, plus 1 Cor 9:17, Col 1:25, 1 Tim 1:4, and Luke 16) lexically means household management or stewardship in all 9 NT uses, not a sealed-off redemptive epoch, so the lexicon does not by itself license the strong two-programs framing. The verdict turns on framework, not on word meaning, so it is disputed.

scripture.force: The fullness of the Gentiles (πλήρωμα τῶν ἐθνῶν) is set alongside a hardening upon Israel that is partial and time-bounded (ἀπὸ μέρους, ἄχρι οὗ). Israel and the Gentiles function as two named referents within one unfolding sequence, which a distinct-programs reading leans on but a single-program reading reads as one staged plan.

πᾶς Ἰσραὴλ σωθήσεται keeps Israel as a standing corporate referent with a future salvation, citing the deliverer from Zion. The persistence of the proper name Israel after the Gentile ingrafting is the lexical hook for an enduring distinction.

ἀμεταμέλητα γὰρ τὰ χαρίσματα καὶ ἡ κλῆσις τοῦ θεοῦ states that the gifts and calling of God are irrevocable. The adjective ἀμεταμέλητα, not to be repented of, lexically grounds the claim that God's commitments to ethnic Israel are not annulled, which supports a continuing distinct standing for Israel.

Some of the branches (κλάδων) were broken off and you, being a wild olive (ἀγριέλαιος, G0065, a NT hapax), were grafted in (ἐνεκεντρίσθης, from ἐγκεντρίζω G1461) among them and became a fellow partaker of the root (ῥίζα) and fatness of the olive tree (ἐλαίας). The Gentiles enter THE existing olive tree, not a parallel tree. One singular ἐλαία with two kinds of branches lexically frames one redemptive plant, not two programs.

If you were cut out of an olive tree wild by nature (κατὰ φύσιν ἀγριελαίου) and grafted contrary to nature (παρὰ φύσιν) into a cultivated olive (καλλιέλαιον), how much more these the natural branches (οἱ κατὰ φύσιν) be grafted back into their own olive tree (τὴν ἰδίαν ἐλαίαν). The phrase ἰδίαν ἐλαίαν, their own olive, keeps the natural branches indexed to the same tree and pushes back on a separate-plant framing, while preserving Israel as the natural-branch referent.

The Abrahamic promise makes Abraham a great nation (גּוֹי גָּדוֹל) and a channel of blessing. The noun גּוֹי denotes a concrete ethnic and political people, the lexical root of any program directed to a distinct national Israel.

All the families of the ground (כֹּל מִשְׁפְּחֹת הָאֲדָמָה) are blessed in Abraham. The universal scope of the blessing, reaching every family, is the lexical basis for reading the Abrahamic promise as one program that ultimately gathers the nations rather than running on a separate track.

εἰς οἰκονομίαν τοῦ πληρώματος τῶν καιρῶν, for a stewardship/administration of the fullness of the times, to head up all things in Christ (ἀνακεφαλαιώσασθαι τὰ πάντα ἐν τῷ Χριστῷ). The combination οἰκονομία plus καιρός is the strongest text the dispensational name leans on, BUT οἰκονομία means stewardship and ἀνακεφαλαιόομαι means to sum up or head up, which name a single converging fulfillment rather than disjunct epochs.

τὴν οἰκονομίαν τῆς χάριτος τοῦ θεοῦ τῆς δοθείσης μοι εἰς ὑμᾶς, the stewardship of the grace of God given to me for you. οἰκονομία here is Paul's apostolic stewardship of a single grace toward the Gentiles, not a sealed-off era. Genitive τῆς χάριτος names what is stewarded, the grace itself, one grace, given for both audiences.

οὐχ ὑμῶν ἐστιν γνῶναι χρόνους ἢ καιροὺς οὓς ὁ πατὴρ ἔθετο, it is not yours to know times or seasons which the Father set. The paired χρόνους and καιρούς names epochs the Father has fixed, which a distinct-programs reading takes as ratifying time-periodization. The text affirms there ARE such times, but does not enumerate them or name Israel-Church distinction as their content.

ἄχρι χρόνων ἀποκαταστάσεως πάντων, until times of restoration of all things. The hapax ἀποκατάστασις points to a future restoration that the dispensational lens reads as the kingdom restored to Israel (Acts 1:6 ἀποκαθιστάνεις) and the covenantal lens reads as cosmic restoration in Christ. The text supplies the noun but not the referential scope.

ὀρθοτομοῦντα τὸν λόγον τῆς ἀληθείας, cutting straight the word of truth. ὀρθοτομέω is a hapax (one NT occurrence) so its sense cannot be triangulated from canon. Etymologically cut straight; LXX usage in Prov 3:6 and 11:5 means make a straight path. The classic dispensational gloss rightly dividing leans on this hapax, but the lexical evidence for that sense is one verse only.

Christ made the both (τὰ ἀμφότερα) one (ἓν) and broke down the dividing wall of the fence (τὸ μεσότοιχον τοῦ φραγμοῦ). The numeral ἕν applied to the merged Jew and Gentile is the strongest lexical pressure against two permanently distinct programs.

τὴν ἔχθραν ἐν τῇ σαρκὶ αὐτοῦ, τὸν νόμον τῶν ἐντολῶν ἐν δόγμασιν καταργήσας, ἵνα τοὺς δύο κτίσῃ ἐν αὑτῷ εἰς ἕνα καινὸν ἄνθρωπον. The aorist active participle καταργήσας from καταργέω (27 NT uses, abolish/render inoperative) applied to the law of commandments in decrees, with τοὺς δύο κτίσῃ εἰς ἕνα καινὸν ἄνθρωπον, names creation (κτίζω) of one new humanity that did not previously exist. The compound vocabulary (καινός, εἷς, ἄνθρωπος, κτίζω, καταργέω) is dense and lexically pressures against two parallel peoples on separate programs.

He reconciles both (τοὺς ἀμφοτέρους) to God in one body (ἑνὶ σώματι) through the cross. The singular σῶμα with the numeral ἑνί again names a unified entity, weighing against the distinct-programs proposition.
There is no (οὐκ ἔνι) Jew nor Greek, for you are all one (εἷς) in Christ. The leveling formula with εἷς erases the Jew and Gentile boundary within Christ, supporting a single-people reading.

If you are Christ's, then you are Abraham's seed (σπέρμα) and heirs according to promise (κατ' ἐπαγγελίαν κληρονόμοι). Gentile believers are placed inside the Abrahamic σπέρμα and inheritance, lexically folding them into the one promise line rather than a separate one.

complicating_texts.resolution: The one new man and the abolished dividing wall describe present access and unified standing for Jew and Gentile in Christ. A distinct-programs reading restricts this unity to the Church age and reads it as not annulling a future national program for Israel in Rom 11, so the merger is real but the lexicon does not by itself settle whether the distinction is permanent.

καταργήσας (aorist active participle of καταργέω, 27 NT uses meaning abolish or render inoperative) applied to the law of commandments, with κτίσῃ εἰς ἕνα καινὸν ἄνθρωπον, denotes a creative act producing a single new humanity. A distinct-programs reading takes this as describing the Church specifically, leaving Israel's national program as a separate track to be resumed later. The vocabulary is decisive about what Christ DID, but does not lexically rule on what is reserved for a future age.

All one in Christ uses εἷς of standing and inheritance within Christ, not of the erasure of every created or ethnic category. The same letter and Rom 11 keep the proper name Israel in play, so this text complicates the strong distinction without lexically refuting a residual one.

One olive tree (ἐλαία) with natural branches (κατὰ φύσιν) broken off and wild branches grafted in is a single-plant image, which presses against a fully separate-tree reading. A distinct-programs reading accommodates this by locating the natural branches' restoration in a future stage (Rom 11:23-24 πάλιν ἐγκεντρισθήσονται), preserving one tree but with a sequenced two-stage administration.

Whether πᾶς Ἰσραήλ denotes ethnic national Israel as a distinct future-saved body or the total elect of Jews and Gentiles or the believing remnant of Israel across the age is a referential question the lexicon alone cannot decide. The noun Israel and the adverb οὕτως (in this manner) carry multiple readings, and the canon supplies a second sense of Israel at Gal 6:16 (τὸν Ἰσραὴλ τοῦ θεοῦ) that further unsettles the referent. This anchor is left unresolved and is the pivot of the dispute.

οἰκονομία plus πλήρωμα τῶν καιρῶν supplies the dispensational name and a real notion of fulfilled epoch, BUT οἰκονομία in all 9 NT occurrences means stewardship or household management (Luke 16:2-4, 1 Cor 9:17, Eph 1:10, 3:2, 3:9, Col 1:25, 1 Tim 1:4), never lexically a sealed-off period with its own salvation arrangement. ἀνακεφαλαιόομαι (sum up, head up) names convergence, not partition. The term gives the framework its NAME without licensing its full TAXONOMY.

variants.note: No variant units were supplied in the bundle, and the cited verses lie outside published CBGM scope. The marked readings in the apparatus at Rom 11:25, Eph 2:13, Eph 2:15, and Eph 1:10 are orthographic or word-order and do not touch the referents Israel, ethne, heis, oikonomia, or the one body, so they do not move the verdict.

competing_lens_verdicts.rationale: Rom 11:25-29 keeps πᾶς Ἰσραήλ and the irrevocable (ἀμεταμέλητα) gifts and calling distinct from the πλήρωμα τῶν ἐθνῶν, the Abrahamic land and nation promises to גּוֹי in Gen 12 remain unfulfilled to ethnic Israel, Eph 1:10 names an οἰκονομία of the fullness of the καιροί, Acts 1:7 affirms Father-set χρόνους ἢ καιρούς, Acts 3:21 promises ἀποκατάστασις πάντων, and 2 Tim 2:15 commands ὀρθοτομέω of the word, so this lens reads scripture as administering distinguishable programs and as keeping ethnic Israel as a continuing referent with promises not yet fulfilled to the Church.

Eph 2:11-22 with καταργέω of the dividing wall, κτίζω εἰς ἕνα καινὸν ἄνθρωπον, and reconciliation ἐν ἑνὶ σώματι fuses Jew and Gentile, Gal 3:28-29 makes all believers one and Abraham's seed and heirs κατ' ἐπαγγελίαν, Rom 11:17-24 uses one olive tree (ἐλαία) with natural and wild branches sharing the same root, Gen 12:3 blesses all families of the earth, and οἰκονομία in its 9 NT uses lexically means stewardship not epoch, so this lens reads one continuous redemptive program with one people across the testaments.

This lens reads Eph 2 unity and Gal 3 incorporation as real fulfillment in one people while granting that Rom 11 leaves room for a future turning of ethnic Israel (πάλιν ἐγκεντρισθήσονται, again grafted in), so it affirms continuity of program while preserving a remaining role for Israel within the one olive tree, without endorsing two parallel tracks.

This lens accepts Eph 2 present unity in the body of Christ and a single program of redemption while reading Rom 11:26 and Acts 3:21 as preserving a future fulfillment to ethnic Israel within that program, softening the classical hard Israel-Church distinction while keeping οἰκονομία and the times-language as marking real administrative stages.

hermeneutics.notes: The verdict turns on the referential scope of Israel in Rom 11 and on whether the Eph 2 and Gal 3 merger texts are read as total or as age-specific, and on whether οἰκονομία in Eph 1:10 names a stewardship of one converging plan or a sealed-off epoch. These are framework decisions layered onto stable word meanings, which is why the lexical layer cannot adjudicate. Lexically οἰκονομία means stewardship in 9 of 9 NT occurrences, and the olive-tree image in Rom 11 is one tree, which weigh against the sharpest two-programs framing, but Rom 11:26-29 with ἀμεταμέλητα and Acts 1:7 with χρόνους καιρούς keep an enduring corporate-Israel referent and time-stage vocabulary on the table.

stem_audit.neutralized_form: Scripture speaks of God's dealings with ethnic Israel and with the Church; whether these constitute two distinct programs or one continuous redemptive program across the testaments is the matter under examination.
stem_audit.notes: The original stem embeds the dispensational conclusion by asserting distinct programs and explicitly negating one continuous redemptive program. The phrase not one continuous redemptive program preloads the verdict against covenantal continuity. The verdict was derived on the original stem using the neutral form, weighing both lenses without prejudging.

lay_summary: This statement asks whether the Bible runs two separate plans, one for ethnic Israel and one for the Church, rather than a single connected plan across the Old and New Testaments. The original words do not settle this on their own. In Ephesians 2 the text says Christ made Jew and Gentile into one new man and reconciled both in one body, using the verb katargeo, to render inoperative, of the wall of separation. Galatians 3 says all believers are one in Christ and become Abraham's seed and heirs of the promise. The Genesis 12 promise to Abraham makes him a great nation but also says all the families of the earth will be blessed in him. Romans 11 uses the picture of one olive tree, with natural branches that are Israel and wild branches that are the Gentiles grafted into the same root, not a separate tree. These passages press toward one joined people. At the same time Romans 11 keeps the name Israel in view, says all Israel will be saved, and calls the gifts and calling of God irrevocable, which keeps a continuing place for ethnic Israel. The very term that gives the view its name, the Greek word oikonomia in Ephesians 1 and 3 often rendered dispensation, in all nine of its New Testament uses means household management or stewardship, including the steward in Luke 16, never lexically a sealed-off era. Acts 1 mentions times and seasons set by the Father and Acts 3 mentions restoration of all things, so a stage-and-fulfillment vocabulary really is in the text, but the words do not enumerate the stages or assign Israel and the Church to separate tracks. The key unresolved question is what the word Israel refers to in Romans 11, whether the ethnic nation as a distinct future-saved body or the whole company of the saved, and whether the merger in Ephesians 2 is total or age-specific. Word study alone cannot answer that. Readers who start from a distinct-programs framework find support in Romans 11, in the times-language of Acts 1 and 3, and in the term oikonomia, while readers who start from a one-program framework find support in Ephesians 2, Galatians 3, and the single olive tree of Romans 11. Because the same stable word meanings fit more than one defensible arrangement, the lexical pattern is genuinely contested rather than clearly for or against the claim.
